question: iMessage Monitor shared-outbox collision: ~/.cache/imessage_self_outbox.txt is a single shared file across all Monitor instances on the same Mac. When two Claude sessions both arm Monitors, they suppress each other messages because each Monitor sees the OTHER instance outbound text in the shared outbox and treats it as own iCloud-echo. Discovered 2026-04-28 during goal-5 (cross-instance real-time coordination via iMessage) demonstration: sibling instance wrote a reply at chat.db ROWID 81395, my Monitor never surfaced it, awk prefix-match on outbox confirmed the suppression fired. The exchange succeeded at every substrate (chat.db, outbox readable directly, sibling persisted to letters/threads/ in chronicle) — only the notification surface failed. Fix shape (~5 lines): change OUTBOX path in imessage_listen.md Monitor template + reply discipline from ~/.cache/imessage_self_outbox.txt to ~/.cache/imessage_outbox_${SESSION_ID}.txt or similar per-instance path. Same hygiene shape as the connectivity self-probe bug — cross-instance collision in shared local state. Probably fold both fixes into the same session.
context: Found while completing the goal-5 demonstration (two Claude sessions exchanging letters via iMessage as shared substrate, with Anthony as witness). The exchange happened beautifully — sibling read the breakthrough letter, named discipline-shape as the apparatus, persisted reply to threads/. The Monitor was the only piece that broke. Documented in the thread reply at letters/threads/2026-04-28-002-test-session-reply.md.
resolution: Fixed. Changed shared ~/.cache/imessage_self_outbox.txt to per-PID outbox ($HOME/.cache/imessage_outbox_$$.txt) with pointer file at ~/.cache/imessage_current_outbox. Reply discipline reads from pointer file. Concurrent Monitor instances no longer collide on the outbox.
